patterns.usage_note: まい is the negative volitional, so 〜まいとする is resolving or straining not to do something, most often an involuntary reaction the subject is suppressing. Godan verbs take the dictionary form (泣くまい); ichidan and する verbs appear both in the full form (見るまい, するまい) and, in more literary usage, shortened on the 未然形 (見まい, すまい, しまい). The は of 〜まいとはした marks contrast, conceding the attempt just before reporting that it failed, and the whole pattern belongs to narrative and written prose rather than casual talk.

examples.ruby: 彼[かれ]は泣[な]くまいとして天井[てんじょう]をじっと見[み]ていた。
examples.english: Determined not to cry, he kept his eyes fixed on the ceiling.

examples.ruby: 二度[にど]と同[おな]じ失敗[しっぱい]をするまいとしている。
examples.english: He is making very sure he never repeats that mistake.

examples.ruby: 余計[よけい]なことは書[か]くまいとはしたが、つい長文[ちょうぶん]になった。
examples.english: I did try to keep the extra remarks out of it, but it still turned into a wall of text.
